subjects.description: small blue rectangular mass attached to the bottom of the vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A blue block attached to a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the center of the frame. The motion starts from a low stretched position and continues bouncing up and down through the clip without being caught or stopped.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel oscillates vertically with period ~0.7 s and shrinking amplitude from ~190 to ~70 pixels, while x stays near zero, so it is a 1D vertical spring around an equilibrium. Candidates go from ideal sine to viscous decay to speed-squared air drag and amplitude-dependent stiffness to test what best extrapolates the decay and period.

critique.finding: The block hangs on a spring swinging with pace {omega} about rest level {s_eq} while light drag {gamma} shrinks the bounces. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a clear patterned wiggle in the misses.

critique.why_it_won: It allows the bounce to fade with speed while the ideal spring cannot fade at all and the extra cubic and quadratic terms change almost nothing.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, its round named before it existed: a linear spring with dry friction and a drive. Muse Wonder read the spectrum tool and wrote the drive itself, at the right frequency; the damping was written as viscous.
finding: A spring bouncing up and down with friction slowing it, while something pushes it rhythmically at a different rate. Measured: natural angular frequency of spring about 9 rad/s; equilibrium position along track about 73 px; viscous damping coefficient about 0.54 1/s.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6606500). The round was named in 078bdc5 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in 3d5237d before the clip was rendered; the run used commit 6514586 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in cd70ce2. Missed under the rule, with the drive found by Muse Wonder. The drawn law was a linear spring with dry (Coulomb) friction and a periodic drive at 11.65 rad/s. Code called Muse Wonder in because the best law missed the frames it was fitted to by 111 times the noise. Muse Wonder called residual_spectrum on Muse Spark's viscous law, read an unexplained peak at 11.74 rad/s (150 times the noise), and wrote a viscous spring with a periodic drive started there; that try was entered for it when its time ran out, and it won: drive frequency 11.720 ± 0.038 rad/s against 11.65 (1.8σ), drive strength 1.64 ± 0.08 m/s² against 1.598 (0.5σ), natural frequency 8.9905 ± 0.016 against 8.9917 (0.1σ). Its damping is viscous (17σ) where the drawn friction is dry, so the term set differs. Code's fallback drive on Muse Spark's law tied second. Code's dry-friction move on the leader never ran: the run was past its 600 s budget. The winner misses the unseen frames by 26 times the noise, against 116 for the best law without a drive. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

si.scale: the render's own scale, 0.00125 m per pixel (orthographic camera)

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - mu sign(x') + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

mu.rule: the swing dies in N half cycles, N uniform in [10, 16] (drawn 11.71); mu = w0^2 A / (2N)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.314)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 1.295)

sealed.narration: a block on a spring, filmed from the side
sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner (Muse Wonder, after its residual_spectrum read): linear (ω), viscous γ = 0.544 ± 0.031 (17σ, present), drive F = 1310 ± 66 px/s² (20σ, present) at ω_d = 11.720 ± 0.038; drawn: linear, Coulomb, drive. Term sets differ: viscous where Coulomb was drawn.

spectrumAtScoring.summary: Residual spectrum of “Damped nonlinear Duffing spring” on the fitted frames (its misses, fitted as sinusoids one at a time, strongest first): strongest at ω = 11.74 rad/s (period 0.535 s), amplitude 150 × the noise (21.2 px in s): UNEXPLAINED, a peak at ω = 11.74 rad/s that is not the motion's frequency, a harmonic, a drift or noise; a periodic drive F·cos(ωt+φ) with ω near this value is the usual cause; a drive whose fitted frequency slides onto the motion's own frequency is not a drive; next at ω = 7.83 rad/s (period 0.803 s), amplitude 39.3 × the noise (5.58 px in s): one of a pair mirrored close about the motion's own frequency with like amplitudes, the motion's own amplitude or frequency changing over the clip (the form of the damping or the stiffness), not a drive; next at ω = 9.95 rad/s (period 0.631 s), amplitude 19.8 × the noise (2.81 px in s): one of a pair mirrored close about the motion's own frequency with like amplitudes, the motion's own amplitude or frequency changing over the clip (the form of the damping or the stiffness), not a drive. The motion's own frequency is 9.03 rad/s.
spectrumAtScoring.note: The labels are the run's own (code 6514586 labelled the spectrum, passed Muse Wonder the labelled summary and a residual_spectrum tool, and held code's drive back as a fallback).
